facts.statement: Beishanlong is the second-largest known ornithomimosaur, exceeded in size only by Deinocheirus.
facts.quote: It is the second-largest ornithomimosaur discovered, only surpassed by the related Deinocheirus.

facts.statement: The genus name Beishanlong combines the Chinese words for "North Mountains" and "dragon".
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to the Bei Shan, the "North Mountains", with a Chinese long, "dragon".

facts.statement: The species name grandis means "large" in Latin, referring to the animal's body size.
facts.quote: The specific name means "large" in Latin, in reference to the body size.

facts.statement: Beishanlong had long arms and legs but lacked the extremely elongated hands, feet, and claws found in later ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The arms and legs were long, though lacking the extremely elongated hands, feet and claws of later forms.

facts.statement: Beishanlong possessed strong forelimbs with 15-centimeter-long claws that were likely excellent for raking or digging the ground.
facts.quote: Las garras de las manos medían 15 centímetros de largo, además poseía fuertes miembros delanteros, que aunque no podría levantar o estirar demasiado habrían sido excelente para rastrillar o excavar el suelo.

facts.statement: The type species Beishanlong grandis was named online in 2009 and formally published in January 2010 by a team including Peter Makovicky, Li Daiqing, Gao Keqin, Matthew Lewin, Gregory Erickson, and Mark Norrell.
facts.quote: The type species is Beishanlong grandis, described and named online in 2009 by a team of Chinese and American paleontologists, and formally published in January 2010 by the same Peter Makovicky, Li Daiqing, Gao Keqin, Matthew Lewin, Gregory Erickson and Mark Norrell.

facts.statement: Beishanlong lived during the late Aptian stage, with fossils found in the Xiagou Formation of the Xinminpu Group.
facts.quote: Beishanlong lived in the late Aptian stage, with its fossils being uncovered in layers of the Xinminpu Group, in the Xiagou Formation.

facts.statement: Beishanlong lived in the middle Cretaceous, approximately 115 to 100 million years ago, between the Aptian and Albian stages in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: un dinosaurio terópodo ornitomimosauriano que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 115 y 100 millones de años, entre el Aptiense y el Albiense en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Beishanlong lived at the boundary of the Aptian and Albian stages, approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Beishanlong vivió en el límite de los estadios aptiano a albiano, hace unos 120 millones de años.

facts.statement: The time range for Beishanlong is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype subadult individual of Beishanlong is estimated to be 5.9 to 7 meters long and weigh between 375 and 626 kilograms.
facts.quote: The size of this subadult individual is estimated at 5.9 - 7 m in length and 375 - 626 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: The found specimen was about 7 meters long and weighed 600 kilograms as a subadult nearing 14 years old, suggesting adults could reach 8 meters and 750 kilograms.
facts.quote: El ejemplar encontrado media cerca de 7 metros de largo y pesaba 600 kilogramos siendo uno de los ornitomimosauriano más grande encontrados aun sin haber alcanzado la madurez con cerca de 14 años de vida y como adulto habría llegado a los 8 metros y 750 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Histological analysis indicates the holotype individual of Beishanlong was still growing when it died, despite being one of the largest definitive ornithomimosaurs described.
facts.quote: According to the description, Beishanlong "is one of the largest definitive ornithomimosaurs yet described, though histological analysis shows that the holotype individual was still growing at its death."

facts.statement: A histological study of the fibula found thirteen or fourteen growth lines, indicating the individual was subadult but growth had already slowed.
facts.quote: Un estudio histológico de la estructura ósea del peroné encontró entre trece o catorce líneas de crecimiento, Indicando que el individuo era subadulto, aunque el crecimiento ya había disminuido.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Beishanlong to Ornithomimosauria in a basal position.
facts.quote: Beishanlong was by the describers assigned to the Ornithomimosauria, in a more basal position.

facts.statement: In 2014, Yuong-Nam Lee et al. recovered Beishanlong as a member of Deinocheiridae, basal to a clade containing Garudimimus and Deinocheirus.
facts.quote: En 2014 Yuong-Nam Lee et al. recuperó a Beishanlong como miembro de Deinocheiridae basal a un clado que contenía Garudimimus y Deinocheirus.

facts.statement: Beishanlong shared territory with Therizinosaurus, Suzhousaurus, and the oviraptorosaurian Gigantoraptor, providing evidence for parallel evolution of gigantism in separate ceratosaurian lineages with beaks and possibly herbivorous diets in a brief period in Central Asia.
facts.quote: Compartió territorio con Therizinosaurus Suzhousaurus y el oviraptorosauriano Gigantoraptor, proporciona la evidencia en la evolución paralela del gigantismo en linajes separados de celurosaurianos con pico y posiblemente herbívoros en un breve período en Asia central.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen FRDC-GS GJ (06) 01-18 was found in 2006 and consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.
facts.quote: El holotipo es FRDC-GS GJ (06) 01-18, fue encontrado en 2006, que consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo.

facts.statement: The paratypes consist of two specimens found in 2007: one with hindlimb remains and another (FRDC-GS JB (07) 01-01) consisting of a pair of pubis bones.
facts.quote: Los paratipos consisten en dos especímenes encontrados en 2007, uno consiste en restos de miembros posteriores, el otro, FRDC-GS JB (07) 01-01, es un par de pubis.

facts.statement: A fourth fossil found in 1999, IVPP V12756 consisting of foot bones, was tentatively referred to the species.
facts.quote: Un cuarto fósil encontrado en 1999, IVPP V12756 que consiste en huesos del pie, fue referido tentativo a la especie.

rejected.statement: Three fossils of Beishanlong were discovered in the early 21st century at the White Ghost Castle site in Gansu province, Northwestern China.
rejected.quote: Three fossils of Beishanlong were found in the early twenty-first century in Northwestern China at the White Ghost Castle site, in the province of Gansu.

rejected.statement: In 2014, Yuong-Nam Lee et al. recovered Beishanlong as a member of Deinocheiridae, basal to a clade containing Garudimimus and Deinocheirus.
rejected.quote: In 2014 Yuong-Nam Lee et al. recovered Beishanlong as a member of Deinocheiridae basal to a clade containing Garudimimus and Deinocheirus.
